# Results — Study 425 (Detrended Price Oscillator) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — the look-ahead-free
DPO(20), `DPO(t) = Close(t) − SMA₂₀(Close)(t)`, turned into a daily **long/flat** position
(long below the −1σ band, flat above the +1σ band, hysteresis between), entered with a
**one-day execution lag**, costs **one-way × turnover**, and raced against buy-and-hold
**excess of cash**. As-of **2026-05-31** (last complete bar 2026-05-29; no partial month).
Daily bars are split- and dividend-**adjusted** (`auto_adjust`, total-return-adjusted).*

## The honest test — DPO long/flat vs buy-and-hold (net of 1 bp, excess of cash)

The fair question for a *timing* rule is not "is it profitable?" (it inherits the market's
drift) but "does it beat simply holding, excess-vs-excess?" The HAC *t* is on the **daily
difference** (strategy-excess − market-excess).

| Ticker | n | exposure | trades/yr | DPO Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | ΔSharpe | ann. edge | HAC *t* (edge) | perm *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** | 8390 | 0.37 | 10.1 | **+0.43** | **+0.65** | **−0.22** | **−5.53%** | **−3.11** | 0.066 |
| QQQ | 6848 | 0.39 | 10.0 | +0.30 | +0.52 | −0.22 | −7.61% | −2.54 | 0.373 |
| IWM | 6540 | 0.42 | 10.2 | +0.27 | +0.47 | −0.20 | −6.17% | −2.32 | 0.455 |
| EFA | 6225 | 0.40 | 9.4 | +0.22 | +0.41 | −0.18 | −4.68% | −2.02 | 0.436 |
| GLD | 5415 | 0.44 | 9.2 | +0.36 | +0.67 | −0.31 | −7.77% | −2.76 | 0.739 |
| DBC | 5110 | 0.48 | 9.2 | −0.08 | +0.21 | −0.29 | −5.16% | −1.85 | 0.928 |

- The DPO rule **underperforms buy-and-hold on every tape** — stocks, tech, small-caps,
  foreign developed, gold and broad commodities. Not one shows a positive Sharpe delta.
- The negative HAC *t*'s are statistically reliable but point the **wrong way**: they
  measure the cost of being out of the market (~60% of the time, in cash) during long
  uptrends, not a reversal/cycle edge.
- The permutation placebo (next section) confirms the *timing* carries no good information:
  on most tapes a random circular shift of the same position beats the real one ~40–90% of
  the time.

## The permutation placebo (SPY) — does the timing carry information?

Holding market returns fixed and circularly shifting the position 2,000 times (preserving
turnover and autocorrelation), the real DPO edge sits in the **left tail**: only
*p* = **0.066** of random shifts are *worse* (i.e. ~93% of random timings beat the real one).
The DPO's specific timing adds nothing positive.

## Cost sweep (SPY long/flat, period 20)

| one-way cost | ΔSharpe | ann. edge | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −0.21 | −5.43% | −3.05 |
| 1.0 bps | −0.22 | −5.53% | −3.11 |
| 2.0 bps | −0.23 | −5.63% | −3.17 |
| 5.0 bps | −0.25 | −5.94% | −3.36 |

The edge is negative **before costs**; at ~10 trades/yr costs add only a sliver. The signal,
not the friction, is the killer — there is no positive break-even cost.

Negative at every window. No corner of the (cost × period) grid is positive.

## Better than the obvious? — DPO vs SMA-cross vs MACD (SPY long/flat, cost 1 bp)

| Rule | ΔSharpe | HAC *t* (edge) |
|---|--:|--:|
| DPO(20) | −0.22 | −3.11 |
| SMA(20/50) cross | −0.13 | −2.76 |
| MACD(12/26/9) | −0.23 | −3.52 |

The DPO's headline pitch is that *detrending makes it special*. It isn't — it lands
middle-of-the-pack among trend-fighting timing rules, all of which give up Sharpe vs holding.

## The look-ahead trap (SPY long/short, cost 0) — honest vs centered DPO

The **textbook** DPO is plotted displaced back `n//2 + 1` bars, so the value at a chart bar
uses bars in its *own future*. A careless backtest that trades that centered series peeks:

| Variant | ΔSharpe | ann. edge | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Look-ahead-free (used in the headline) | −0.60 | −11.14% | −3.14 |
| Centered / peeking (textbook draw) | −0.52 | −9.70% | −2.40 |

Here the peeking version is the *less bad* of the two (the band-state rule swamps the small
leak) — but **both still lose** to buy-and-hold. Even a look-ahead head start can't make the
cycle rule pay. The headline uses only the honest contemporaneous DPO.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's a cycle to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a **planted sinusoidal
cycle** (period 20), the same DPO long/short engine recovers the edge cleanly and reads
~0/negative when nothing is planted:

| Planted cycle amplitude | ΔSharpe | ann. edge | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (random walk) | −0.69 | −12.01% | −1.88 |
| 0.02 (faint cycle) | +0.68 | +12.58% | +1.54 |
| 0.05 (clear cycle) | **+3.68** | +88.08% | **+6.28** |
| 0.10 (strong cycle) | +7.98 | +275.79% | +11.78 |

The engine is a faithful cycle detector. The real-tape verdict is therefore a statement
about the **market** (modern tapes carry no tradable short cycle of this flavour), not the
method.

## Survivorship note

The basket is **liquid ETFs/indices**, not a stock cross-section — there is no
single-name survivorship selection on the Signal axis. The one caveat is the usual *index*
survivorship (SPY/QQQ track surviving-constituent indices), which if anything *strengthens*
the buy-and-hold benchmark the DPO rule is failing to beat — so it cannot manufacture the
negative verdict.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** DPO long/flat nets +0.43 Sharpe vs buy-and-hold +0.65 on SPY
  (−5.53%/yr); daily excess-vs-excess HAC *t* = −3.11 — significant but **wrong-signed**.
  Negative on all six tapes; no positive edge exists.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A structural loser before costs at every cost and every window;
  ~10 trades/yr means costs are not the cause — the rule is.
- **Isolates a tradable cycle? — BUSTED.** Permutation *p* = 0.066 (left tail); no better
  than a plain SMA-cross; the detrending surfaces no tradable rhythm on real tapes. The
  synthetic control proves the engine *would* find a cycle if one were there.
